attributes.residual: THE FRAME-DELTA FRAMING IS AN ARTIFACT; THE REAL GAP IS MISSING C++ EXCEPTION-HANDLING CODEGEN, AND IT IS NOT CLOSEABLE PER-FUNCTION. The superseded record read fndiff's 'frame delta -8 -> our frame is BIGGER; drop 8B of pad/locals' as a pad-sizing problem and proposed an 8-byte ruler applied to this pair. The aligned disassembly refutes that outright: the TARGET IS LARGER, NOT SMALLER - target 32 instructions vs our 26 - and the extra bytes are exception-handling scaffolding, not locals. Target prologue `stmw r30,40(r1)` saves r30 AND r31 and then establishes a FRAME POINTER with `addi r31,r1,0`, addressing the frame through r31 thereafter; it carries a cleanup path our build has no trace of (`addi r3,r31,16` / `bl __unexpected` / `b .`); and it tears down through the alias and the back chain (`mr r12,r31`, `lwz r0,52(r31)`, `lmw r30,40(r12)`, `lwz r1,0(r1)`). Our C compile emits a plain `stw r31,44(r1)` / `lwz r31,44(r1)` / `addi r1,r1,48` frame with no frame pointer, no __unexpected edge and no back-chain restore. dtor_800DBB94 measures IDENTICALLY (target 52 insns vs our 55, `addi r31,r1,0`, `bl __unexpected`, and `lmw r28,40(r12)` restoring through the alias), so the pair really is one mechanism - just not the one recorded. CONSEQUENCE: the existing `u8 unused[24]` / `u8 unused[32]` pads in these two bodies are standing in for the EH frame area, and shrinking them by 8 would chase the measuring instrument rather than the gap. The genuine fix is whole-TU: movieplayer.c is C++ in the original (its own file header cites MoviePlayer.cpp and the assert string at 0x80117684) but is built as .c with cflags_demo, so the EH scaffolding cannot be emitted from any per-function source edit. Route both dtors into the queued movieplayer .cpp conversion, where exceptions-on codegen is the single change that can produce __unexpected edges and frame-pointer prologues; re-measure the pair only after that conversion. NO SOURCE PROBE WAS SPENT, deliberately - the measurement made every available per-function axis provably irrelevant.
attributes.scope: src/game/movie/movieplayer.c::dtor_800DB21C (and its twin dtor_800DBB94, recorded separately). NO source change - read-only measurement; working tree clean. Neither dtor is webfrank-pinned. Note regnorm cannot resolve either symbol (trailing _<ADDR> suffix) and slotdiff inherits that limitation - 'missing: dtor_800DB21C (target: False, ours: False)'; fnasm --diff and fndiff both resolve them, and the aligned fnasm view is the tool that settled this.
